Ridge Roll Rules

Roll three dice and climb one of seven ridges per turn. Roll on as long as you dare - if a roll does not fit your ridge, the climbing of the turn is lost. Camps and summits bring points.

The rules

The board
Seven ridges for the sum of two dice: 2 to 4 (15 steps), 5 (8), 6 (9), 7 (10), 8 (7), 9 (6) and 10 to 12 (6). The low ridges are longer because there the third die is usually big. Every ridge has a hut and a crevasse.
Your turn
Tap "Roll the dice": three dice are rolled. Each die can be the step die - 1 or 2: one step, 3 or 4: two, 5 or 6: three - while the other two give the ridge by their sum. The buttons show these ways; choose one.
One ridge per turn
With the first roll of a turn you choose the ridge (not one whose top you have already reached). From then on every roll must fit this ridge again.
Turn lost
If a roll has no way up your ridge, the turn is lost: the climbing of this turn is gone, your camps stay.
Hut and crevasse
If your climber reached the hut in this turn, a lost turn still leaves you a camp at the hut. Landing exactly on the crevasse sends the climber two steps back (never below your camp); jumping over it does nothing.
Making camp
After every good roll you may stop: your climber becomes your camp, and next time you start from there. A camp is your own black marker (circle, square, triangle or star); the climber of this turn is a white ring with a thick black edge.
The top
Whoever makes camp at a top first gets 6 extra points, everybody later 3. The ridge stays open for the others.
Winning
Every step of your camps is a point, plus the summit points. When somebody reaches the target (30 or 45, chosen before the game), the round is played to the end so that everyone had the same number of turns. Then the most points win; players level on points win together.
Who starts
Who starts is drawn by lot.
The computer
Easy takes the way with the most steps and stops after two good rolls. Medium and Hard reckon whether one more roll is worth the risk; Hard also aims for the summit points.

Example

You roll 5, 2 and 4. The ways: 2 + 4 = 6 with the 5 as step die (ridge 6, three up), 5 + 4 = 9 with the 2 (ridge 9, one up), 5 + 2 = 7 with the 4 (ridge 7, two up). You take ridge 6, three up. Next roll 1, 3, 3: 3 + 3 = 6 with the 1 fits - one more step. Then you stop: your camp is on step 4 of ridge 6.
